title: I Was a Wandering Sheep
description: I Was a Wandering Sheep in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Horatius Bonar wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 105.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: I was a wan-dering sheep, I did not love the fold; I did not love my Shep-herd’s_ voice, I would not be con-trolled; I was a way-ward child, I did not love my home; I did not love my Fa-ther’s voice, I loved a-far to roam.

lines: I did not love the fold;
I did not love my Shepherd’s voice,
I did not love my home;
I did not love my Father’s voice,
They followed me o’er vale and hill,
They found me nigh to death,
They bound me with the bands of love,
’Twas He that washed me in His blood,
’Twas He that brought me to the fold,
But now I love my Shepherd’s voice,
I love, I love, the fold.
But now I love my Father’s voice,
I love, I love, His home.

licence: Public domain: Horatius Bonar died in 1889.
credits: Words by Horatius Bonar (1808–1889), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
